prompt: Please generate an image. Locked painterly style: hand-painted stylized game art, chunky readable shapes, detail painted not modelled, mid-level detail, softer muted colours with gentle saturation, epic and luminous, never grim. The palette's warm gold and cool teal are painted into the surfaces, but the light is flat, even studio light: no strong key light, no cast shadows, no rim light. Use the attached images only as reference as described: the first attachment is always the style reference for palette and brushwork; later attachments are the approved designs to keep. Material swatch sheet, wide landscape 16:9, plain light neutral grey background. Square swatch tiles in a neat grid, evenly spaced, each flat-on (orthographic, no perspective, no horizon, no shadows from outside the tile), a seamless tileable painterly texture with edges that would wrap, broad clumped brushwork, no tiny high-frequency noise, a short neat label under each. Swatches: Redraw of the attached reference sheet to the current spec: keep exactly the same swatches, their order and their materials. Crag biome terrain, four square tiles in one row, labels exactly as written in quotes: "Alpine Turf" (seen straight down with no block sides showing, thin patchy short wind-flattened green-gold turf with grey-blue cragslate showing through, a few lichen spots and tiny alpine flowers); "Grit Path" (a close-up of packed grey-brown grit with small flat cragslate stones, filling the entire tile evenly; the tile is all grit, it is not a picture of a path, no turf strips on either side, seen straight down with no block sides showing); "Cragslate Cliff" (grey-blue layered cragslate face with sharp parallel diagonal strata, flat chunky painted planes, a little lichen, no ore seams); "Cragslate Underside" (darker, cooler grey-blue stepped cragslate strata with a cool teal wash, no ore seams). Each tile is one evenly spread texture filling the whole square edge to edge, seen straight on with no perspective, no horizon, no focal point, no border, no single path or band crossing it and no light gradient, so its left edge would wrap onto its right and its top onto its bottom. Title at the top: "Crag terrain".
